overview.description: Kout Bo 6 (or simply Koutbo6) is a high-stakes, team-based trick-taking game popular in Egypt, Kuwait, and across the Arab world. Played by two teams of three (6 players total), it utilizes 54 cards (standard 52 + 2 Jokers). It is a game of bidding, where the winning team's contract (Hokm) dictates the trump suit, and the Red and Black Jokers serve as the most powerful permanent trumps.

history.origins: Developed in the mid-20th century in the Levant and Gulf regions. It is an expansion of the Lebanese game 'Kout', adapted for larger social groups of 6 people.
timeline: 1950s: Kout variants spread through the Eastern Mediterranean.
1970s: The 6-player team version (Kout Bo 6) becomes the competitive standard in Kuwait and Egypt.
2010s: Online platforms like Jawaker popularize Koutbo6 globally.
Present: One of the most played card games in Middle Eastern social clubs.
history.evolution: The game evolved to include a 'Mulzum' (Must) rule where the dealer is forced to bid if everyone else passes, ensuring competitive play every round.
history.cultural: In Egyptian culture, Koutbo6 is a game of intense communication and 'trash talk' between the two competing teams.

setup.players: 6 players in two teams of 3. Teammates sit in alternating positions (A1, B1, A2, B2, A3, B3).
setup.dealing: Each player receives 9 cards. Dealing and play are counter-clockwise.

rules.objective: As the bidding team, fulfill your contract (win the number of tricks bid). As the defenders, prevent them from doing so.
rules.gameplay:
1. Must follow suit. If unable, play any card.
2. Jokers can be played even if a player HAS the suit led.
3. Leading a Joker forces all other players to play a Trump card if they have one.
keyRules: Must follow suit when able; if void may play any card including trump or Joker.
Jokers may be played to an existing trick anytime; leading a Joker has restrictions (bid 8/9 or trump face cards played).
High bidder declares trump (Hokm); Red and Black Jokers are permanent trumps, Color Joker highest.
Bid 5 (Bab) to 9 (Bawan); if first five pass, dealer must bid at least 5 (Malzom).
First to 101 points wins; or 51+ vs 0; or Bawan made on first hand.

strategy.basic: If your team has two out of the three top cards (Red Joker, Trump Ace, Black Joker), bid at least 7. The probability of losing a trick is low when you control the 'Master Trio'.
strategy.intermediate: Team Coordination: Since you have two partners, watch who wins the early tricks. If partner A1 wins with a King, don't waste your Queen to 'over-win'; save it for the next round to exhaust the opponent's cards.
strategy.advanced: The Joker Lead: Lead the Black Joker if you want to flush out the Red Joker early. This clears the way for your Trump Ace to become the most powerful remaining card.
tips: Never bid 'Bawan' (9) unless your team has at least 5 of the 9 trumps and both Jokers.
Communication (within rules) is key. Watch your partners' discards to see which suits they are void in.

difficulty.easy: Fails to follow suit; uses Jokers at the wrong time; poor bidding.
difficulty.medium: Excellent team-play coordination; understands Joker hierarchy.
difficulty.hard: Expert at trick-counting; accurately predicts opponents' Joker locations; master of the 'Mulzum' defense.

phases.label: Bidding
phases.notes: Player to dealer's right bids first. Bid 5 (Bab) to 9 (Bawan) or pass. If first five pass, dealer must bid at least 5 (Malzom). High bidder declares trump (Hokm).

phases.label: Play tricks
phases.notes: High bidder leads first. Winner of each trick leads next. Follow suit; if void may play any. Jokers have lead restrictions.

play_card.description: Play one card to the current trick. Must follow suit if possible; if void may play any card including trump or a Joker. Jokers may be played to an existing trick anytime; leading a Joker is allowed only if your team bid 8 or 9, or after Ace-K-Q-J of trump are played.
play_card.constraints: Must follow suit when able. When leading a Joker, must satisfy bid-8/9 or trump-face-cards-played condition.

draw.reason: This game has no draw-from-stock action.

pass.description: Pass (decline to bid) when it is your turn in the bidding round.
pass.constraints: Only legal during the bidding phase when it is your turn to bid.

bid.description: Bid a number of tricks (5 to 9) your team will attempt to win. Five is Bab, nine is Bawan. Your bid must be higher than any previous bid this hand. High bidder becomes maker and declares the trump suit (Hokm).
bid.constraints: Bid must be between 5 and 9 and higher than current high bid. If first five players pass, dealer must bid at least 5 (Malzom).

trumpConfig.trumpSuitRanking: Color Joker highest, then Black-White Joker, then Trump Ace, then A-K-Q-J-10-9-8-7-6-5-4-3-2.
trumpConfig.overtakingRule: Trump Ace ranks second only to Color Joker when trump suit is declared.

trickConfig.leadRestrictions: Joker may not lead except if team bid 8 or 9, or after Ace-K-Q-J of trump are played.

edgeCases.text: Malzom: If the first five players all pass, the dealer must bid at least 5.
Joker may be led only if the team bid 8 or 9, or after Ace, King, Queen, and Jack of trump have been played.
If a Joker is led illegally, it cannot win the trick; the next card played determines the suit for the trick.

customActions.description: Deal 9 cards to each player, one at a time, counter-clockwise starting from the player to dealer's right.
customActions.constraints: Dealer only. Deck is cut by player to dealer's left before dealing.

engine.handRankingSystem: Trick ranking: Color Joker, Black-White Joker, Trump Ace, then A-K-Q-J-10-9-8-7-6-5-4-3-2. No poker hand evaluation.
engine.rankingSystem: Color Joker highest, Black-White Joker, Trump Ace, then Ace down to 2 in trump and led suit.
engine.deckDescription: Standard 52-card French deck plus two distinguishable Jokers (Color Joker and Black-White Joker). The two Jokers are permanent trumps; Color Joker is highest, Black-White Joker second. Four suits: Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs, Spades; thirteen ranks each: Ace, 2 through 10, Jack, Queen, King.
engine.suitDescription: Four traditional French suits: Hearts (Cœur), Diamonds (Carreau), Clubs (Trèfle), and Spades (Pique), each represented with standard French card iconography and distinct color coding for easy identification.
engine.rankDescription: Standard thirteen ranks per suit: Ace, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, Jack, Queen, and King, where each rank has distinct value and meaning depending on the specific game rules and player strategies.
engine.dealPattern: 9 cards each, one at a time, counter-clockwise from right of dealer.
